question: Why did the checkout error rate jump on 12 March?

contributing_factors.description: Checkout v2.14 deployed to eu-west lowered the payment client timeout from 5s to 500ms, so slow payment calls began to fail.
why_chain: Checkout requests failed more often in eu-west.
Calls to the payment service timed out.
The client timeout was lowered from 5s to 500ms.
The new default came in with checkout v2.14.
The release had no load test against realistic payment latency.

ruled_out.reason: Request volume stayed within 3% of the previous week.

evidence.summary: Error rate rose from 0.4% to 3.1% at 14:05 (change point).
92% of the extra errors come from checkout in eu-west; other regions are flat.
checkout v2.14 rolled out to eu-west at 14:02.
Request volume within 3% of the same hour last week.

reasons: The deploy happened 3 minutes before the change point.
Logs and config record independently point to the same timeout.
The main alternative (traffic spike) is ruled out by the data.
missing_data: Payment service latency metrics would confirm how many calls exceed 500ms.

actions.action: Roll back payment_client.timeout_ms to 5000 in eu-west.
Add a release check that flags timeout changes below the p99 latency of the called service.
Roll out checkout releases to one region at a time with automatic rollback on error-rate alerts.
